request.title: Show running paces per kilometre
request.body: Runners outside the US think in minutes per kilometre. In src/runPaces.js, let callers ask for paces per kilometre. formatPace(secPerMile, unit) and paceTarget(zones, intensity, unit) take an optional unit, "mi" or "km", which is "mi" when left out. With "km", formatPace returns the pace per kilometre for the same speed, so 483 seconds per mile is "5:00", and the label paceTarget returns shows kilometre paces and ends in "/km". paceTarget still returns secPerMile unchanged, so stored values keep their unit. Any other unit is treated as "mi". Add an exported helper secPerKm(secPerMile) that converts a pace to seconds per kilometre and returns null for anything that is not a positive number. Everything that works today must keep working: existing callers need no changes and the existing tests pass as they are.

artifact.title: Running Pace Kilometre Support
artifact.problem: Runners outside the US primarily use minutes per kilometre for pace tracking, but the current system defaults to and primarily supports miles, limiting accessibility for international users.
goals: Enable the formatting of running paces in kilometres per minute.
Provide a utility to convert seconds per mile to seconds per kilometre.
Maintain complete backward compatibility for existing mile-based calculations and callers.
nonGoals: Changing how pace data is stored in the database.
Adding a user-facing settings toggle to switch units (this is a logic-layer update for callers).
constraints: Existing callers must function without modification.
The unit 'mi' must remain the default if no unit is provided.
Stored values must remain in seconds per mile (secPerMile) regardless of display unit.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When formatPace is called with a value of 483 seconds per mile and the unit 'km', it returns the string '5:00'.
When formatPace is called without a unit (or with 'mi'), it returns the pace formatted as minutes per mile.
When formatPace is called with a unit other than 'km' or 'mi', it treats the unit as 'mi' and returns the pace formatted as minutes per mile.
When paceTarget is called with the unit 'km', the returned label contains kilometre paces and ends with the string '/km'.
When paceTarget is called with the unit 'km', the returned numerical pace value remains in seconds per mile (secPerMile).
When paceTarget is called without a unit, the returned label uses mile-based formatting.
When secPerKm is called with a positive number representing seconds per mile, it returns the equivalent seconds per kilometre.
When secPerKm is called with a non-positive number (0 or negative) or a non-number value, it returns null.

artifact.approach: Update `src/runPaces.js` to introduce a conversion utility `secPerKm` and modify `formatPace` and `paceTarget` to accept an optional `unit` parameter. To maintain backward compatibility, `unit` defaults to `'mi'`. The internal logic and return values for `paceTarget` will continue to use `secPerMile` as required by the constraints, converting to kilometers only for the display string (the label).

components.name: Run Pace Utilities
components.responsibility: Provide mathematical conversion and string formatting for running paces in both miles and kilometers.

decisions.title: Default Unit Value
decisions.decision: Implement `unit = 'mi'` as the default parameter for `formatPace` and `paceTarget`.
decisions.rationale: Ensures existing callers in `RacePlanPanel.jsx` and `runPlanGenerator.js` continue to function without modification, satisfying the backward compatibility constraint.

decisions.title: Conversion Logic Placement
decisions.decision: Perform kilometer conversion only inside `formatPace` and `secPerKm`, keeping `paceTarget`'s numeric output in `secPerMile`.
decisions.rationale: Complies with AC-5 and the constraint that stored/returned numerical values must remain in seconds per mile.

decisions.title: Fallback Unit Handling
decisions.decision: Treat any `unit` argument that is not exactly `'km'` as `'mi'`.

decisions.title: Input Validation for secPerKm
decisions.decision: Use the existing `finitePositive` utility internally within `secPerKm` to ensure only positive numbers are processed, returning null otherwise.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with the existing architectural pattern in `runPaces.js` (lines 53-56) and satisfies AC-8.

risks: Rounding errors: Since `formatPace` uses `Math.round`, the sequence of converting `secPerMile` -> `secPerKm` -> `Math.round` must be precise to avoid 1-second discrepancies compared to expectations.

reason: the work has no user interface

defects.description: The `secPerKm` function is incorrectly allowing strings that can be coerced into numbers (e.g., "483"), whereas AC-8 requires it to return null for non-number values. The actual behavior is that `secPerKm("483")` returns a numeric result instead of null.

reasons: The `secPerKm` function is incorrectly allowing strings that can be coerced into numbers (e.g., "483"), whereas AC-8 requires it to return null for non-number values. The actual behavior is that `secPerKm("483")` returns a numeric result instead of null.

artifact.summary: Fix secPerKm to return null for non-number values as per AC-8 by adding a type check before calling finitePositive.

artifact.title: Support Kilometre Pace Formatting
artifact.summary: Introduces the ability to format running paces in minutes per kilometre while maintaining backward compatibility by keeping internal calculations and storage in seconds per mile.
changes: Updated `formatPace` to support 'km' and 'mi' units, including conversion logic from seconds per mile to seconds per kilometre.
Updated `paceTarget` to support optional units, allowing the display label to reflect '/km' while preserving the underlying `secPerMile` numeric value.
Implemented `secPerKm` utility to convert seconds per mile to seconds per kilometre, including input validation to return null for non-positive or non-number values.
risks: Since the underlying data remains in seconds per mile, any new callers must explicitly pass 'km' to `formatPace` and `paceTarget` to avoid defaulting to mile-based formatting.
